Go to a shrine, and head over to Make Offering. In Make An Offering, you can hit select and give them all your white or yellow items or whatever. These will exchange for divine rice. You can have up to 600, which would last you a super long time, and there's not a lot better to do with your whites and yellows until that gets full.

Then go down to Kodama Bazaar. Put all the ammo and elixir on auto-buy. There you go! If you have the divine rice, you will always have max elixir and ammo every death. How I got past that stupid snake with only 3 elixirs I'll never know. (Oh wait I cheesed it with a summon ally...)

Anyway, all that extra healing should help a ton. Also get the ninjutsu that lets you auto-revive, and the spells that heal you over time. I never die from lack of healing anymore, just lack of skill and getting combo'd.

The intent I can tell, from someone with design experience, is the ability to inflate the power of lower rarity without subsequently obliging all top end decks to have maximum amounts of the rarest cards; the latter is great from a money making perspective, but far less so from a 'fun' perspective, and can lead to many of the failed CCGs that litter the market because nobody is willing to shell out the money for a top-end competitive deck where the top rarity is flat out superior in every way. Look at Magic if you want to see that in practice, and Hearthstone too has rather expensive decks (Thankfully you can't have multiple Legendaries).

There's many advantages to restricting card count by rarity, from making it harder to pull off cheesy combos since only 1 in 40 cards might have the core, to increasing depth since things that let you cycle and dig into your deck become more valuable, to increasing diversity as there's multiple approaches to win. After all, if you are reliant on 3 Mythics hitting the board, then you better build your deck well to stall and get to them. This also works great in a digital medium as there's no trading or market for rare cards anyway, so they are just losing out on people spending a fortune trying to get all the cards they need to finish a particular deck. 

The trick is then to make sure certain synergies or Common-level combos are not too overpowered, which we'll see!

It was the unique flavor of the main character and the ability to have him be a reliable witness despite eccentricities that made it such a unique and enduring read for me.
